summary: kb repair-aliases' engine. Distinct from kb repair's missing-identity-aliases check (that one catches notes with NO aliases; this is for aliases that EXIST but no longer describe the file/flow — a note rewritten several times can carry identity-shaped words that were really symptoms of an earlier write). planAliasRepair(root, offset, limit) paginates every active file/flow note (never lessons), and for each one re-folds its raw log with {capIdentity:false} to compute hiddenIdentityAliases = the full historical union minus what's currently in the capped render — showing an agent what a blind retract would silently resurface (capAliases operates on the union minus retractions, not "the visible 12 minus what was removed"). aliasRepairWorklist renders the batching + never-retract-without-reading-the-current-code instructions inline, same self-describing-worklist discipline as repair.ts's repairWorklist — CLI, MCP, and all three host wrappers render this same text, never restate it.

summary: kb repair-aliases' engine. Distinct from kb repair's missing-identity-aliases check (that one catches notes with NO aliases; this is for aliases that EXIST but no longer describe the file/flow). planAliasRepair(root, offset, limit) paginates every active file/flow note, computing hiddenIdentityAliases via {capIdentity:false} so an agent sees what a blind retract would resurface. 2026-08-02 FIX: the command had no memory of 'already reviewed' — a note judged still-accurate reappeared on every future run forever, since that judgment left no trace (unlike kb repair's mechanical checks). Fixed with FoldedNote.aliasesVerifiedAtEdit (fold.ts): eligible now excludes a note where nothing has changed since its stamp. USER caught the real trap before this shipped: naively filtering that way breaks pagination, because `eligible` shrinks as notes get marked verified, so continuing to advance --offset by the page size (the OLD documented flow) silently skips whatever slides into that position next. Fix changed the RESUME CONTRACT, not the slicing: mark a batch verified, then re-run with offset 0 (default) — reviewed notes are simply gone from the list. offset/nextOffset still work for read-only browsing, just are no longer how you advance through a reconciling pass. Verified end to end same session: backfilled aliasesVerified:true onto all 53 notes this repo had already reconciled; kb repair-aliases now correctly reports 'No file/flow notes to reconcile.'
